We're eager to hear your thoughts on how you would approach this project and any innovative solutions you might propose.Thank you for considering our request. We look forward to your expertise in developing a solution that aligns with our vision.

title: C++ Task: Pipelined RISC-V CPU Simulator

This functionality will be instrumental in planning and decision-making processes, allowing for precise adjustments to work schedules, resource allocation, or project scope as needed to ensure timely and efficient project delivery. title: Expert Go Developer with Real-Time Data Processing and (some) Financial Market Skills
description: API : https://github.com/polygon-io/client-goTo ensure the accuracy and reliability of our system, it is crucial to manage system time effectively, particularly in addressing time drift. This entails continuous synchronization with an NTP (Network Time Protocol) server to maintain alignment with global time standards. Once we know the Timedrift and our latency we can also use timestamps of incoming data to align continuously as the timestamp will be based on the exchange which is very precise.For data acquisition, we leverage both the Polygon API (available via Go or RESTful interfaces). The process is initiated by specifying a target date, for example, 2024-02-16, to the Go program. Utilizing the API, the system retrieves all option contracts for "O:SPXW" (excluding "SPX" optiosn) expiring on the specified date, with strike prices within a 5% range above and below the current market value.Additionally, the API facilitates querying the last known index price for "I:SPX", providing a reference for market conditions to be able to get that 10% above or below.From the retrieved data, we expect to isolate approximately 100-150 contracts expiring on the given day. Subsequently, the system establishes a connection to the WebSocket for real-time data streaming or utilizes the Go API for the same purpose, encompassing all relevant contracts. utilizing both our system clock and time stamps from incoming data we can move forward in 500ms increments.We begin by aggregating data points every 500 milliseconds, starting at 9:30:00.000, capturing both the first quote and the initial index point of the trading session. It's important to note that we are dealing with real-time quotes, utilizing the last available quote closest to 9:29:59.9999 for our initial data point. Additionally, index data is published every second, allowing us to potentially use these timestamps to monitor and adjust for any clock drift, as they are issued precisely every second.An example of the data format we receive is as follows:"ask_exchange": 302,"ask_price": 9.8,"ask_size": 3,"bid_exchange": 302,"bid_price": 9.4,"bid_size": 1,"sequence_number": 303635,"sip_timestamp": 1708034398285329200For each of the 100+ contracts, we calculate the midpoint price by averaging the ask_price and bid_price. This value serves as our reference for further calculations. To determine the option's delta, we first need to compute the implied volatility (IV) using a fast bisection method. This calculated IV is then inputted into the Black-Scholes model to compute the delta for each option. I have an example wrote in GO for both of these as guidelines, but might need further optimization.After calculating IV / delta for all options, we organize them to identify those closest to a delta of 0.50 for calls and -0.50 for puts, which indicates options at or near the money.print the put and call option closest to closest abs to .50 delta to terminal showing latency

title: Anova/ Ancova
description: InstructionsAn interventional study was conducted to determine the effects of three treatments (exposure) on a health measurement which is measured on a continuous scale. Let’s assume this was a double-blind randomized study and all participants were equally motivated to comply with the intervention arm to which they were assigned. The health measure was collected from each participant at the start of the trial and at the end of the trial. The study outcome was the difference between the measurements before and after the treatment was given and calculated as [measurement at end] – [measurement at start].Create a poster with appropriate tables, figures, and results.Invent a research question, including the health condition and treatment/intervention.InstructionsDetermine whether there were significant differences among the means of ‘Difference’ across the three treatments. You will use SAS Studio for your ANOVA (and maybe ANCOVA) analyses.The dataset has the following variables:• Difference: (Y), the difference between the health measurement taken at two points, post-treatment and pre-treatment. It is calculated as [post treatment – pre-treatment]. This is your study outcome, or independent, variable.• Factor:â€¯An independent variable (X).• Treatment (or intervention):â€¯Three treatments: A, B, and C. This is your study exposure variable. In ANOVA and ANCOVA, this is your categorical variable.Complete the following tasks:1. Conduct an exploratory analysis of Difference and Factor.2. Conduct an exploratory analysis of Difference and Factor stratified by Treatment.3. Create descriptive tables for the results of steps 1 and 2.Consider your mode of communication and create accordingly.4. Check for assumptions: Equal sample sizes of each group, normal distributions, variances are equal across groups, and check for collinearity of Difference and Factor. Assume samples are independent.5. Determine the best analysis plan for measuring whether the effect of three levels of treatment on the means of Difference differed. Include plots. You should decide whether to include ‘Factor’ as a covariate.6. Create at least one figure using a Graphs task.Consider your mode of communication and create accordingly.7. Execute your analysis plan.8. Create a poster, presentation to communicate the objective, intervention arms, methods, results, and interpretation/application. Include appropriate figures and/or tables.Provide:• Poster slide(s)• SAS output

title: Data Analysis
description: Certainly! Data analysis is a process of inspecting, cleaning, transforming, and modeling data with the goal of discovering useful information, drawing conclusions, and supporting decision-making. Here are some key steps and concepts involved in data analysis:1. **Define Objectives:**- Clearly define the goals and objectives of your analysis. What do you want to achieve? What questions are you trying to answer?2. **Data Collection:**- Gather relevant data from various sources. This could be from databases, surveys, sensors, APIs, etc.3. **Data Cleaning:**- Preprocess and clean the data to handle missing values, outliers, and inconsistencies. This step is crucial to ensure the accuracy and reliability of your analysis.4. **Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA):**- Explore the data using descriptive statistics, visualizations, and summary tables to understand its structure, patterns, and relationships. This step helps in generating hypotheses and insights.5. **Data Transformation:**- Transform the data if needed, such as scaling, normalizing, encoding categorical variables, or creating new features.6. **Statistical Analysis:**- Apply statistical methods to test hypotheses, identify patterns, and make inferences about the population based on sample data.7. **Machine Learning:**- Implement machine learning algorithms for predictive modeling or classification tasks, depending on the nature of your analysis.8. **Data Visualization:**- Create visual representations of the data using charts, graphs, and dashboards to communicate insights effectively.9. **Interpretation and Conclusion:**- Draw conclusions from the analysis and interpret the results in the context of your objectives. Communicate findings in a clear and understandable manner.10. **Documentation:**- Document your analysis process, methodologies, and results. This is essential for reproducibility and for others to understand and validate your work.11. **Feedback and Iteration:**- Seek feedback from stakeholders and iterate on your analysis if needed. Continuous improvement is crucial in data analysis.Popular tools for data analysis include Python with libraries like Pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib, R, and tools like SQL for database queries. Additionally, specialized tools such as Excel, Tableau, and Jupyter Notebooks are commonly used in the field.

Note – We are using Power BI Pro License.One thing we tried, to minimize the data (by taking only last 6 month of data), and after making these changes, we didn’t face same issue in Power BI Service.But right now we are not looking into solution where we have to minimize the data.
